questions.statement: Which sentence works best as a thesis statement in an opinion essay?
questions.context: Lucia is starting her opinion essay about school canteens with a clear position.

options.text: This essay argues that canteens should serve healthy food.
options.feedback: Correct! This essay argues that canteens should serve healthy food correctly states a clear position, so it works perfectly as a thesis for the introduction.
The option I had lunch at noon is wrong because I had lunch at noon merely reports a personal fact, which takes no position and cannot guide an argument.
The option Canteens are rooms with tables is wrong because Canteens are rooms with tables only defines a place factually, which offers no opinion to argue.
The option Many students eat every day is wrong because Many students eat every day states a general habit without stance, so it cannot anchor an opinion essay.

questions.explanation: A thesis statement presents the writer position clearly in the introduction, usually in one sentence. It guides the whole essay and previews reasons. Without a thesis, readers cannot follow the argument direction.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which structure best organizes an argumentative opinion essay about phones?
questions.context: Diego is organizing his essay about phones into introduction, body, and conclusion.

options.feedback: The option joke, song, drawing, goodbye is wrong because joke, song, drawing, goodbye lists unrelated creative pieces, which provides no logical frame for building an argument.
The option date, name, signature only is wrong because date, name, signature only describes letter formatting, which misses introduction, reasons, and conclusion entirely.
Correct! Introduction, arguments, counterargument, conclusion correctly orders the essay, so it gives Diego a logical frame for presenting phone views persuasively.
The option title plus ten random facts is wrong because title plus ten random facts piles unconnected data, which lacks stance, links, and paragraph purpose.

questions.explanation: A standard opinion essay uses introduction with thesis, two or three body paragraphs with one idea each, and conclusion restating the position. This frame keeps arguments ordered and easy to follow for B2 readers.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which option lists FORMAL linkers suitable for an argumentative essay? Note the question asks for formal register.
questions.context: Carmen is choosing formal linking words for her essay about tourism.

options.feedback: The option Moreover is wrong as informal because Moreover is actually formal and academic, so it cannot serve as an example of casual spoken linking.
The option stuff and things is wrong for formal writing because stuff and things is vague spoken vocabulary, which lowers the academic tone required in essays.
The option plus more ideas is wrong because plus more ideas is conversational and loose, which fails to link sentences with the precision expected formally.
Correct! However and Furthermore correctly exemplify formal essay linkers, so they perfectly suit Carmen academic paragraph about tourism effects.

questions.explanation: Formal essay linkers include Moreover, Furthermore, However, In contrast, Consequently. They connect ideas between sentences and show addition, contrast, or result. Informal fillers like plus or stuff weaken academic tone.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence works best as a topic sentence for a paragraph about library benefits?
questions.context: Pablo writes a body paragraph about libraries and needs a strong topic sentence.

options.feedback: The option Libraries first opened long ago is wrong because Libraries first opened long ago gives history only, which does not state the paragraph argument about present benefits.

options.text: Libraries improve learning by offering free resources.
options.feedback: Correct! Libraries improve learning by offering free resources correctly states the paragraph main idea, so every later sentence can support it with reasons and examples.

options.text: I like the blue chairs inside.
options.feedback: The option I like the blue chairs inside is wrong because I like the blue chairs inside offers a tiny personal detail, which is too narrow to control a full paragraph.
The option This essay has four paragraphs is wrong because This essay has four paragraphs describes overall structure, which belongs in planning rather than opening a body paragraph.

questions.explanation: A topic sentence states the main idea of one paragraph clearly at its start. All later sentences support it with reasons and examples. General thesis or tiny detail sentences cannot control a single paragraph.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence best supports the claim that sport helps students? Choose evidence.
questions.context: Sara must add a reason with evidence to support her claim about sport.

options.text: Sport is good because it is good.
options.feedback: The option Sport is good because it is good is wrong because Sport is good because it is good merely repeats the claim in a circle, which provides no evidence at all.

options.text: Sport reduces stress, for example a school study found calmer pupils.
options.feedback: Correct! Sport reduces stress, for example a school study found calmer pupils correctly adds concrete evidence, so it strongly supports the claim about sport benefits.
The option Everyone knows sport is nice is wrong because Everyone knows sport is nice appeals to vague popularity, which offers no verifiable data or concrete example.

options.text: I love sport very much indeed.
options.feedback: The option I love sport very much indeed is wrong because I love sport very much indeed states personal feeling only, which cannot prove a general benefit for readers.

questions.explanation: Strong support pairs a reason with concrete evidence like data, expert voice, or observed example. Bare repetition of the claim proves nothing. For example plus a specific study result makes argument credible at B2.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence best introduces a counterargument about school uniforms fairly?
questions.context: Jorge must present an opposing view fairly before answering it in his essay.

options.text: Some argue uniforms remove style, which is a valid concern.
options.feedback: Correct! Some argue uniforms remove style, which is a valid concern correctly states the opposition fairly, so Jorge can then answer it with a respectful rebuttal.

options.text: Opponents are fools with bad ideas.
options.feedback: The option Opponents are fools with bad ideas is wrong because Opponents are fools with bad ideas insults people instead of ideas, which destroys fair and balanced argument.
The option Nobody ever disagrees with me is wrong because Nobody ever disagrees with me denies that opposition exists, which removes any chance to show balance.
The option Uniforms are blue and cheap is wrong because Uniforms are blue and cheap lists neutral facts, which presents no opposing argument to address.

questions.explanation: A counterargument paragraph fairly states the other side with Some argue that or Critics claim. It shows balance before rebuttal. Ignoring or insulting the opposition weakens credibility and argument depth.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence best rebuts the worry that exams create too much pressure?
questions.context: Elena writes a reply that answers the counterargument about exam pressure.

options.text: Exams are hard, so I quit.
options.feedback: The option Exams are hard, so I quit is wrong because Exams are hard, so I quit surrenders to the counterargument completely, which abandons the writer original position.

options.text: Although pressure exists, clear schedules reduce it effectively.
options.feedback: Correct! Although pressure exists, clear schedules reduce it effectively correctly concedes then overturns, so it forms a strong rebuttal that answers the concern with a solution.

options.text: Exams are exams and that is that.
options.feedback: The option Exams are exams and that is that is wrong because Exams are exams and that is that merely repeats the noun without reasoning, which refutes nothing at all.

options.text: Pressure is bad, exams are bad.
options.feedback: The option Pressure is bad, exams are bad is wrong because Pressure is bad, exams are bad only restates negativity in parallel, which offers no contrasting solution or evidence.

questions.explanation: A rebuttal concedes partly then overturns with However or Nevertheless plus stronger reason. Pattern: admit plus contrast plus evidence. Pure surrender or pure repetition misses the refutation move taught for opinion essays.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence works best as a concluding restatement for the parks essay?
questions.context: Raul must close his essay about parks with a strong final paragraph.

options.feedback: The option Parks have trees and benches is wrong because Parks have trees and benches only describes features factually, which restates no position and summarizes no argument.

options.text: I will visit the park tomorrow.
options.feedback: The option I will visit the park tomorrow is wrong because I will visit the park tomorrow announces a personal plan, which adds new action rather than closing the argument.

options.text: In short, parks deserve funding because they improve health.
options.feedback: Correct! In short, parks deserve funding because they improve health correctly restates the stance and summarizes the benefit, so it closes the essay about parks strongly.

options.text: Parks were built in nineteen ninety.
options.feedback: The option Parks were built in nineteen ninety is wrong because Parks were built in nineteen ninety gives historical data only, which neither restates the thesis nor concludes persuasively.

questions.explanation: A conclusion restates the thesis in new words, summarizes main points briefly, and may add a recommendation. It introduces no new argument. Copying the introduction word for word or adding fresh claims weakens closure.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses a formal register appropriate for an essay about phones?
questions.context: Nora must fix an informal sentence so it suits a formal opinion essay.

options.text: School is gonna be cool stuff.
options.feedback: The option School is gonna be cool stuff is wrong because School is gonna be cool stuff uses slang gonna and cool stuff, which is chatty and unsuitable for formal essays.
The option I dunno, exams whatever, bye is wrong because I dunno, exams whatever, bye mixes slang and indifference, which violates formal academic tone completely.

options.text: Kids gotta chill with phones lol.
options.feedback: The option Kids gotta chill with phones lol is wrong because Kids gotta chill with phones lol uses slang gotta and lol, which belongs in messages rather than essays.

options.text: Schools should therefore limit phone use.
options.feedback: Correct! Schools should therefore limit phone use correctly uses formal vocabulary and structure, so it perfectly suits the academic tone of an opinion essay.

questions.explanation: Formal register avoids contractions, slang, and chat fillers. Replace gonna with going to, kids with children, plus with Moreover. Formal vocabulary plus full forms raises the essay tone to academic B2 standard.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which opening hook best catches readers for an essay on screen time?
questions.context: Iker reviews four hooks and keeps the one that opens an essay best.

options.feedback: The option Hi, how are you today is wrong because Hi, how are you today is a casual greeting, which catches no interest and suits chat rather than essay openings.

options.text: Did you know teens spend four hours daily online?
options.feedback: Correct! Did you know teens spend four hours daily online correctly opens with a striking fact as a question, so it hooks readers before the thesis on screen time.
The option This essay has five paragraphs is wrong because This essay has five paragraphs merely counts structure, which bores readers and wastes the opening impact.

options.text: I will write about phones now.
options.feedback: The option I will write about phones now is wrong because I will write about phones now announces intent flatly, which lacks surprise or curiosity to engage readers.

questions.explanation: A hook opens with a striking fact, question, or scenario to catch interest before the thesis. Rhetorical questions or surprising data work well. Greetings or thesis copies waste the opening impact.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement correctly describes the function of essay linkers?
questions.context: Alba compares linkers that show contrast versus linkers that show cause.

options.text: However signals contrast while Consequently signals result.
options.feedback: Correct! However signals contrast while Consequently signals result correctly separates functions, so Alba can classify linkers by logical meaning rather than mere position.
The option However means because exactly is wrong because However means because exactly confuses contrast with cause, which mislabels the core logical function completely.
The option Consequently contrasts two ideas is wrong because Consequently contrasts two ideas mistakes a result marker for opposition, which reverses its true function.
The option Because shows sharp contrast is wrong because Because shows sharp contrast claims a cause word opposes ideas, which contradicts its explanatory purpose.

questions.explanation: Contrast linkers include However, Although, In contrast, Despite. Cause linkers include Because, Since, Consequently, Due to. Mixing the sets confuses logic. Identifying function by meaning, not position, ensures coherence.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which order best builds a body paragraph about daily reading benefits?
questions.context: Hugo must order four sentences into a logical body paragraph about reading.

options.feedback: The option example, conclusion, topic, explanation is wrong because example, conclusion, topic, explanation buries the main idea in third place, which confuses the reader progression badly.
The option conclusion first then all details is wrong because conclusion first then all details closes before arguing, which leaves explanation and example without a guiding claim.
Correct! Topic, explanation, example, concluding link correctly sequences the paragraph, so the claim about reading leads naturally through support to closure.
The option random facts without any link is wrong because random facts without any link piles disconnected data, which provides no hierarchy or logical movement at all.

questions.explanation: Logical paragraph order runs topic sentence, explanation, example, concluding link. Claim first, then why, then proof, then tie back. Random orders bury the main idea and confuse the reader progression.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which paragraph best shows unity around the idea of home recycling? It must stay focused.
questions.context: Leire must spot which paragraph stays on one idea about recycling.

options.feedback: The option paragraph about buses, lunch, games is wrong because paragraph about buses, lunch, games mixes three topics, which breaks unity and confuses the recycling focus.

options.text: paragraph where all sentences explain sorting waste
options.feedback: Correct! Paragraph where all sentences explain sorting waste correctly keeps unity, because every sentence supports the single idea of sorting waste at home.

options.text: paragraph with jokes and song lyrics
options.feedback: The option paragraph with jokes and song lyrics is wrong because paragraph with jokes and song lyrics adds entertaining digressions, which drift away from the stated recycling idea.
The option paragraph listing random city names is wrong because paragraph listing random city names piles unrelated geography, which offers no support for the recycling claim.

questions.explanation: Unity means every sentence supports the single topic sentence idea. Digressions about lunch or football break unity even if grammatical. Checking each sentence against the main idea keeps paragraphs focused and persuasive.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the formal linker Moreover correctly in an essay about bikes?
questions.context: Mario checks four uses of Moreover to find the only correct placement.

options.feedback: The option Bikes help health, moreover cheap is wrong because Bikes help health, moreover cheap joins clauses with only a comma and drops grammar, which misuses the formal linker.

options.text: Moreover cheap bikes good for all.
options.feedback: The option Moreover cheap bikes good for all is wrong because Moreover cheap bikes good for all omits the verb and comma, which makes the sentence fragmentary and incorrect.

options.text: Bikes cut pollution. Moreover, they save money.
options.feedback: Correct! Bikes cut pollution. Moreover, they save money correctly places Moreover at a new sentence with a comma, so it adds the second benefit formally and grammatically.
The option Bikes moreover because cheap health is wrong because Bikes moreover because cheap health stacks linkers without logic, which creates a confused and ungrammatical string.

questions.explanation: Moreover starts a new sentence or follows a semicolon to add a formal point, always with a comma after it. It cannot join two clauses with only a comma. Moreover plus comma signals continuation of the same argument.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which phrase best replaces vague language with precise essay vocabulary about health?
questions.context: Clara must replace vague wording with precise academic vocabulary in her draft.

options.feedback: The option nice good cool stuff is wrong because nice good cool stuff piles vague praise words, which lack precision and lower the academic tone badly.
The option very very big problem indeed is wrong because very very big problem indeed stacks intensifiers without exactness, which sounds spoken rather than academic.
The option bad things are bad stuff is wrong because bad things are bad stuff repeats vagueness in a circle, which conveys no precise evaluation for readers.
Correct! Significant benefit for public health correctly uses precise academic vocabulary, so it sharpens the claim and raises the essay formality appropriately.

questions.explanation: Precise essay vocabulary replaces vague nice, bad, big with beneficial, harmful, significant. Exact adjectives sharpen claims and raise formality. Vague intensifiers like very very add length without meaning.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: An essay argued for banning cars downtown. Which conclusion move is correct?
questions.context: Adrian compares two conclusions to see which avoids adding new arguments.

options.text: restates ban plus summarizes health and cost
options.feedback: Correct! Restates ban plus summarizes health and cost correctly closes without novelty, because every word traces back to arguments already developed in the body.
The option adds solar panels never discussed is wrong as a model because adds solar panels never discussed introduces a fresh topic at the end, which breaks the closure rule badly.

options.text: asks ten new questions at end
options.feedback: The option asks ten new questions at end is wrong because asks ten new questions at end opens fresh inquiry rather than summarizing, which leaves the essay unresolved.
The option apologizes and says forget essay is wrong because apologizes and says forget essay abandons the stance entirely, which neither restates nor summarizes the argument.

questions.explanation: Strong conclusions summarize without new claims. Introducing solar panels in the last line breaks closure rules. The test is whether each conclusion word traces back to body ideas already argued.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which version correctly fixes the run on sentence about social media effects?
questions.context: Aitor must fix a run on sentence in his draft about social media.

options.text: Social media connects us it harms sleep.
options.feedback: The option Social media connects us it harms sleep is wrong because Social media connects us it harms sleep jams two clauses without punctuation, which forms a classic run on error.

options.text: Social media connects us, it harms sleep too.
options.feedback: The option Social media connects us, it harms sleep too is wrong in formal writing because the comma alone cannot join two main clauses, so the splice remains incorrect.

options.text: Social media connects us. However, it harms sleep.
options.feedback: Correct! Social media connects us. However, it harms sleep correctly splits with a period and linker, so it fixes the run on while showing contrast clearly.

options.text: Social media sleep connects harms us it.
options.feedback: The option Social media sleep connects harms us it is wrong because Social media sleep connects harms us it scrambles word order, which destroys both grammar and meaning.

questions.explanation: Run on sentences jam two main clauses without proper punctuation or linker. Split with a period or join with However plus comma or Because. Correct sentence boundaries keep complex arguments readable for examiners.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which ordering principle makes three uniform arguments most persuasive in an essay?
questions.context: Nerea must choose the most persuasive order for three arguments about uniforms.

options.feedback: The option weakest last so essay fades is wrong because weakest last so essay fades ends on the least convincing point, which lets persuasive energy collapse before the conclusion.
The option random order without any plan is wrong because random order without any plan scatters impact unpredictably, which prevents building toward a memorable climax.
The option longest sentence always first is wrong because longest sentence always first confuses length with strength, which misorders logic and buries the best point early.
Correct! Strongest argument last for climax correctly saves the best point for the end, so the essay builds momentum and peaks just before the conclusion.

questions.explanation: Persuasive order often saves the strongest argument for last, creating a climax before the conclusion. Weaker points open, mid points build, strongest closes. Ending weakly lets the essay fade instead of peaking.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which description shows a complete and well controlled opinion essay? Choose the full set.
questions.context: Unai must decide which essay shows full argumentative control at B2 level.

options.feedback: The option single paragraph of slang jokes is wrong because single paragraph of slang jokes lacks thesis, structure, evidence, and formality, so it shows almost no argumentative control.
The option list of dates without opinion is wrong because list of dates without opinion reports facts only, which contains no stance, reasons, or persuasive organization at all.
The option copied chat messages as essay is wrong because copied chat messages as essay imports informal fragments, which ignore structure, evidence, and academic register completely.

options.text: thesis plus reasons plus counterargument plus conclusion
options.feedback: Correct! Thesis plus reasons plus counterargument plus conclusion correctly names all pillars, so it demonstrates full argumentative control expected at B2 level writing.

questions.explanation: Full control combines clear thesis, linked paragraphs, evidence, counterargument plus rebuttal, formal tone, and restated conclusion. Missing any pillar weakens the whole. Holistic checklists train self revision better than single rule focus.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the best revision move to turn the chatty draft into a formal essay?
questions.context: Ane edits a weak draft where every sentence starts with And then into academic form.

options.feedback: The option keep every And then forever is wrong because keep every And then forever preserves monotonous spoken chaining, which keeps the draft chatty and unstructured.
The option add ten exclamation marks instead is wrong because add ten exclamation marks instead substitutes punctuation for structure, which adds noise without building logical argument.
The option delete all verbs from draft is wrong because delete all verbs from draft destroys grammatical sentences entirely, which makes revision impossible and meaning collapse.

options.text: replace with Firstly, In addition, Consequently
options.feedback: Correct! Replace with Firstly, In addition, Consequently correctly varies formal connectors, so it transforms repetitive narration into structured academic argument.

questions.explanation: Academic revision replaces repetitive And then with varied linkers like Firstly, In addition, Consequently, In conclusion. Sentence variety plus formal connectors transforms chatty narration into structured argument. This final polish separates basic from mastery writing.
questions.subject: ingles
